sentences.text:
2. Heard Sri G.Yaswanth, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Md.Farooq, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home.
3. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home would submit that, in Crime No. 141 of 2025,
the petitioners were served with a notice under Section 35(3) of the BNSS, in connection with a case registered against them for the offence under Section 498A IPC.
Learned Assistant Government Pleader would further submit that another case has also been lodged against the petitioners.
Apart from the 498A case, a counter case in Crime No. 142 of 2025 has also been registered and is pending against the petitioners, in relation to which they were called to the police station.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the police are frequently calling the petitioners to the police station and making them to wait in the police station for whole day.
5. In that view, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
However, Police are directed to follow due process of law to secure the presence of the petitioners if any specific purpose regarding the crimes registered against the petitioners.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
_ _ _ Dr.JUSTICE VENKATA JYOTHIRMAI PRATAPA Date:07.11.2025
